svg.title: Legacy ambiguity is preserved before migration
svg.desc: Current files use Git conflicts. Legacy forks stop normalization until an author preserves and combines their intent; no timestamp chooses content.
svg.text: Legacy ambiguity is preserved before migration
Current files use Git conflicts. Legacy forks stop normalization until an author preserves and combines their

g.text: Legacy selected content
A single legacy leaf can be projected for a compatibility read.
Current publications contain one editable complete value.
Legacy branch candidates
Legacy packages may contain independently authored branch
definitions; the compatibility loader retains all candidates.
No fabricated winner
Current-file conflicts belong to Git. When legacy content is
ambiguous, the loader exposes every head and leaves current
content unavailable.
No implicit inheritance
Convenience story edits refuse ambiguous legacy content instead
of inheriting fields from an arbitrary candidate.
Explicit content resolution
Preserve candidates in Git, explicitly combine their intent,
then publish/select complete current content before
normalization. No new Saga parent graph is authored.
One current publication
Normalization produces current.json only after exact pin
conversion is prepared; obsolete sources are cleaned after
publication. Git retains committed earlier content.

svg.text: Stable identities · exact evidence pins · Git-owned committed history
